summary: ClearView is evaluating where to run embeddings/rerank: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary constraints: sub-80ms p95 latency for rerank path, cost per 1M queries, data residency and audit log requirements. Customer leans toward hosted for speed to prod but wants a private/Dedicated fallback for regulated customers. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-25 16:30 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Ortega (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (ClearView Head of Search), Ethan Cole (Platform Eng), Priya Narang (ML Eng)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Marta (ClearView): yes, loud and clear. thanks Samir.
[00:07] Samir: great quick agenda — understand your current infra for retrieval/rerank, constraints on latency and cost, and walk hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private) plus a sketch of a benchmark. Lina will jump in on perf details.
[00:20] Lina (Redwood SE): hi all, quick note — i might jump between screens to show a sample perf table later, but mostly we can talk numbers.
[00:26] Marta: perfect. context: we power search and answer flows for enterprise analytics — about 12M docs, a mix of text and short tables. our typical query pattern: user asks a natural language question, we do retrieval (vdb) top 100 then rerank top 10 with a cross-encoder or light LLM scoring. need p95 rerank end-to-end under 80ms ideally. cost is also a big factor — we have to estimate 1-3M queries/month for pilot then scale.
[00:52] Priya (ML Eng): adding that some customers are regulated — data residency and audit trails are required. we also prefer not to send raw doc content to third-party models for some customers.
[01:02] Samir: understood. so two axes: latency/throughput and privacy/compliance. wanted to ask first — are you currently hosting embeddings in your VPC (self-hosted vector store) or using a managed vdb?
[01:12] Ethan: we currently run an in-house ES + vector plugin cluster and a small qdrant proof, but we've seen consistency and ops issues at scale. we'd like to avoid reinventing the serving layer if possible.
[01:24] Lina: common tradeoff — hosted Redwood API gives fastest time-to-value; dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; private gives control for regulated customers but requires more ops. for rerank p95 <80ms, we usually recommend colocating the reranker near the vdb or using a dedicated path with short KV cache warmup.
[01:42] Marta: can you unpack the 'colocate' part — we plan to keep vector store in our VPC for residency. does hosted Redwood incur cross-VPC network hops for rerank?
[01:50] Lina: good question. with hosted we've seen two patterns: 1) customers push embeddings to a managed VDB like Pinecone and call Redwood Hosted for rerank via API — network overhead depends on where vdb is. 2) customers use Redwood Private or Dedicated with a connector running in their VPC so rerank is local. for strict residency and <80ms you would probably need a dedicated or private deployment near the VDB or bring the VDB into the same cloud region.
[02:15] Priya: ok — so for pilot we could do hosted for non-regulated tenants and private for regulated. latency wise do you have sample numbers for 128-dim vs 512-dim embeddings when doing hybrid fanout + rerank?
[02:28] Lina: rough numbers — these are workload dependent but ballpark: embeddings encode size affects vector DB IO and ML scoring. for a 128-dim vector we see lower memory bandwidth; a typical pipeline (retrieve top 100 then rerank top 10) with Hosted Redwood using a medium instance gets p95 rerank ~60-100ms depending on region and kv cache hit. for 512-dim it increases cost and tail. if you need strict p95 <80ms at 1k qps, dedicated GPUs with batch-friendly kernels or a private deployment is safer.
[03:02] Marta: are those measurements with KV caching / prefix caching enabled?
[03:06] Lina: yes medium instances assume caching. without cache it can be 2x-3x worse. also batch size and continuous batching strategy matters — bigger batch improves throughput but increases tail latency.
[03:18] Ethan: on the ops side we worry about embedding storage cost. if we store 512-dim for all docs vs 128-dim how much difference are we looking at?
[03:26] Lina: storage roughly scales linearly — 4x the size going from 128->512. but we've seen similar retrieval quality improvements plateau after certain dims for many tasks — often 128-256 is sweet spot for semantic search depending on embed model. for rerank you might keep a smaller candidate embed and rerank with a heavier cross-encoder only on top candidates.
[03:47] Priya: for rerank chain, do people run the cross-encoder in the same infra as the embed service? like can Redwood run both scoring and cross-encoder as part of the rerank?
[03:55] Samir: yes Redwood can run scoring as part of the inference chain — you can compose calls: embed retrieval -> rerank model -> final scorer. we support streaming and function-like chaining. for heavy cross-encoders we recommend Dedicated with reserved GPU to hit stable SLOs.
[04:09] Marta: how does integration with our existing vector DB look — we use an in-house vector service now, but we could try Qdrant or Pinecone for the pilot.
[04:18] Lina: integration patterns: 1) Bring your VDB and call Redwood Hosted for rerank (requests hop out). 2) Use Redwood connector (runs in your VPC) that pulls embeddings or scores locally, works with Dedicated or Private. 3) Push your embeddings into Redwood-managed VDB if you want everything managed. For a pilot, the easiest is to connect via API to your VDB and do a small workload. For latency sensitive tenants we recommend a connector or private deployment.
[04:46] Ethan: about fallback routing — if dedicated pool is saturated do you have automatic fallback to hosted?
[04:51] Lina: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants/hosted pool. you can configure policy: strict isolation (no fallback) or graceful degrade (fallback to smaller model or queued requests).
[05:02] Marta: security — do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) and audit logs for private?
[05:06] Samir: yes Private supports customer KMS/HSM integration and detailed audit logs; Dedicated also offers audit trail options but with Redwood-managed keys unless you opt for KMS integration.
[05:16] Priya: about benchmark — we want to measure 1k qps peak with mixed reads (retrieval fanout 100 + rerank top 10), two embed dims (128, 512), and both hosted vs dedicated with fallback. can Redwood outline the runner?
[05:29] Lina: proposed runner: 1) synthetic traffic generator that simulates retrieval+rerank patterns at target qps and tail distributions; 2) three scenarios: Hosted (us-east), Dedicated small pool (reserved), Private connector in your dev VPC; 3) measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 100k queries. we'll provide the script and reproduce steps.
[05:49] Ethan: about data, for regulated flows we'll need to ensure the rerank never sends full doc contents to hosted models. is there a way to mask or only send embeddings?
[05:57] Lina: yes you can configure the pipeline to only send embeddings/ids to hosted endpoints and do rerank on the dedicated/private path. there are also filtering hooks to redact content before sending.
[06:07] Marta: what's the expected ramp time to get a Dedicated pool? if pilot looks good and we sign, how long to get reserved capacity?
[06:12] Samir: typical lead time depends on capacity and sizing — small dedicated pools can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks; larger enterprise reservations are a sales-assisted procurement workflow, often 4-8 weeks including network setup. Private deployments take longer due to networking and KMS integration — typically 6-12 weeks.
[06:30] Priya: any gotchas on quantization — we plan to quantize models for cost. does Redwood support 4-bit or 8-bit inference paths for rerank models?
[06:38] Lina: our runtime supports quantization-friendly execution and 8-bit is common; 4-bit is experimental for some architectures — we'll surface expected RTF (response-time factor) and quality delta. for rerank you need to test quality regression.
[06:51] Marta: ok great. next steps and owners?
[06:54] Samir: recap: Samir will send pricing and a TCO sheet; Lina will send benchmark plan and runner script; Ethan will validate compliance and VPC access; Marta will share internal stakeholders. then schedule a tech deep-dive week of Dec 6.
[07:07] Marta: sounds good, thank you both.
[07:10] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[07:13] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has minor mis-hears — e.g., 'qdrant proof' may be 'qdrant proof-of-concept' and some product names abbreviated. There was a brief audio glitch at ~00:50 where a sentence overlapped.
